newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel business leaders say rate cut not enough.
newsitem.headline: Israel business leaders say rate cut not enough.

text.p: Israeli business leaders said the central bank's decision to cut its key lending rate by 0.3 percentage point was a step in the right direction but far from enough.
The latest cut will bring the key lending rate in October to an annualised 15.5 percent.
Dan Propper, president of the Manufacturers Association, said in a statement that at least another two percentage points must be cut.

Danny Gillerman, head of the Federation of Israeli Chambers of Commerce, also called for a two point cut in interest rates. He criticised what he called the central bank's "zig-zag policy" and said interest rates should change every quarter and not every month. He said the current policy fosters uncertainty and destabilises the economy.
Propper said the Bank of Israel's policy had led to an "absurd situation" whereby the central bank in the past few weeks has injected shekels to buy foreign currency and government bonds.
"In practice the Bank of Israel itself is generating inflationary action," Propper said.
The Bank of Israel has been buying foreign currency to prevent the shekel from strengthening beyond its permitted trading band.
It bought bonds in August to support sagging bond prices.
Propper said the Bank of Israel was concerned only with inflation and not with other economic goals such as export-led growth and preventing unemployment.

Propper said the high level of interest rates could put the Israeli economy on the brink of a crisis and he called for an economic programme that would include a substantial interest rate reduction, a correction in the foreign currency market and a cut in the government's budget.
The central bank maintains that it cannot cut interest rates further unless the government reduces its budget deficit, which is likely to reach 12 billion shekels or more in 1996.
